blocks.text: Condo buildings in Sumas Prairie

There is no condo stock in Sumas Prairie — stated plainly at the top. Sumas Prairie is the low agricultural prairie in southeast Abbotsford, in the City of Abbotsford, between Abbotsford and Chilliwack. Its September 2026 board row records zero attached listings and zero attached sales, no condo or townhome card appeared in its feed, and no named strata complex on the prairie was confirmed on any official or developer source. Plan currency note. Abbotsford's current Official Community Plan is Abbotsforward 2050, adopted December 2025 — the 2016 OCP is NOT current, and any document citing it as the governing plan is a plan out of date.
Streets, schools and getting around Sumas Prairie

items.t: Sumas Prairie is an FVREB board sub-area of the City of Abbotsford — the low agricultural prairie in southeast Abbotsford between Abbotsford and Chilliwack, plus the upland fringe the feed itself surfaces (Majuba Hill / Old Yale Road cards labelled Sumas Prairie). The live page works to Highway 1 (Whatcom Road Exit 95, Cole Road Exit 99, No. 3 Road Exit 104, and Flood Hope Road/Yarrow Exit 109), Sumas Way (Highway 11), Vye Road, Marion Road, Keith Wilson Road and Campbell Road, and describes commercial dairy, poultry, turf, vegetable and berry farms, country home sites along Marion Road, Boundary Road and Arnold, and rural residential homes near Kilgard. Street-level board boundary: UNVERIFIED — FVREB publishes no street-level boundary for the sub-area, and no municipal boundary was substituted for it.

Watershed geography: Sumas Prairie sits in the Sumas River watershed; the Sumas River Watershed Flood Mitigation Planning Initiative's six signatories are the Province of B.C., the Semá:th, Máthxwi and Leq'á:mel First Nations, the City of Abbotsford and the City of Chilliwack.

That is a near-empty row: no sales in either split, and no pace or price conclusion can be drawn from it. SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, so there is no Sumas Prairie median: UNVERIFIED at sub-area level.

What the visible feed actually showed: cards read in full were all labelled "Sumas Prairie" — a Majuba Hill custom acreage house, a 19.49-acre farm parcel offered as Land with barns, a hillside acreage house, a 20-acre farm property and an Arnold-community acreage rancher — an acreage-and-farm feed spanning the prairie floor and its upland edges, with no condo or townhome card in the page text read. The feed's total size is UNVERIFIED.

The middle and secondary schools the live page names sit outside the prairie in the city. Catchments are address-based through SD34's School Locator, and no locator run for a Sumas Prairie address is on record, so catchment schools for any specific address are UNVERIFIED.
Both page claims are UNVERIFIED as stated.

Flood — the defining fact of this sub-area: the City hosts the Province's release on the Sumas River Watershed Flood Mitigation Planning Initiative, signed in April 2023 in response to widespread flooding on Sumas Prairie from heavy rainfall in November 2021; the Province is providing $3.3 million for critical design and assessment work, and has provided approximately $220 million in recovery, preparedness and mitigation funding for Abbotsford and Sumas Prairie since 2021, including $76.6 million for upgrades to the Barrowtown Pump Station. The same release records that December flooding in the Sumas region again demonstrated the corridor is highly prone to water surges, and that the initiative's studies are at various stages of completion — flood mitigation for the prairie is active planning, not a settled fix.
Health care is outside the sub-area: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Rd, and the Abbotsford Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 2692 Clearbrook Rd #100.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Sumas Prairie

items.t: ALR residences cannot be stratified — the rule that leads this section, because it is why the prairie has no condo stock: On land in the Agricultural Land Reserve, a residence cannot be turned into strata lots (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). A prairie farmhouse is a house on land under the ALC residence frame, permanently — it cannot be strata-subdivided into condo units, and no ALR parcel is condo stock.

The ALC housing frame on ALR parcels: land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional residence; the principal residence must have a total floor area of 500 m² or less; a secondary suite is permitted in the ALR only within the principal residence; and an additional detached residence may be up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less and up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha. ALR status for any specific Sumas Prairie parcel: UNVERIFIED — check parcel by parcel.

Zoning frame: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 applies city-wide, including its agricultural zones. The City's AgRefresh parcel-size work records a minimum subdivision lot area of 8.0 ha in the Agricultural One Zone (A1) and 16.0 ha in the Agricultural Two Zone (A2) — so most prairie parcels cannot be split further in any form, strata or fee-simple. The zone of any specific parcel is a per-parcel check: UNVERIFIED for any individual parcel.

Suites and coach/garden suites: under Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014, a secondary suite must be less than 50% of the size of the principal unit, and garden suites and coach houses may occupy up to 15% of the lot area to a maximum of 100 m² — subject on ALR land to the ALC frame above (suite only within the principal residence).
City plan: the current Official Community Plan is Abbotsforward 2050, adopted December 2025 (see the currency note at the top) — the 2016 OCP is not current.

The strata rules, for contrast — they bite only if the same buyer buys strata in urban Abbotsford: Form B (Strata Property Act s. 59) states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance, and a summary of the strata's insurance, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Depreciation reports: since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must obtain one every five years, no deferral by vote. Minimum CRF contribution: at least 10% of the operating fund since November 1, 2023. Rental-restriction bylaws are void since November 24, 2022. 55+ bylaws: SPA ss. 123.1/123.2 — only 55+ is lawful, with exemptions for younger spouse/partner, live-in caregiver, legacy residents and defined child cases (May 1, 2023 expansion). None of this applies to a prairie farm purchase, because there is no strata corporation.

GST and taxes on a prairie purchase: 5% GST applies to new construction, not resales — prairie stock is resale farm/residential product. The First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate (Bill C-4) rebates 100% of GST up to a $1 million price (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5 million, for agreements signed on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031; CRA's Excise and GST/HST News No. 122 states Bill C-4 received Royal Assent on March 13, 2026. The older GST New Housing Rebate (36%, maximum $6,300, $350,000–$450,000 phase-out) still exists. Property Transfer Tax (BC): 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million, 3% above $2 million, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3 million; First-Time Home Buyers' Program full exemption on the first $500,000 at fair market value $835,000 or less, partial $835,000–$860,000; Newly Built Home Exemption full to $1,100,000, partial to $1,150,000.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), if a park home elsewhere is compared instead: pad-rent increases are capped at 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027. No park is verified on the prairie.

blocks.text: Good to know about Sumas Prairie

items.t: The zero is structural, not a slow month. Sumas Prairie's attached row is empty because its land base is farm land under an ALR frame that bars stratification outright — a buyer waiting for a prairie condo project is waiting for a form the governing rules do not produce.
The live page gets both of the prairie's own schools wrong, in two different ways. A buyer using the page's names and address will not find either school.

The flood-mitigation money is real, and the plan is still unfinished. Approximately $220 million in provincial funding since 2021 and $76.6 million for the Barrowtown Pump Station sound like a settled fix; the City-hosted release is explicit that the initiative's hydraulic model, risk assessment, ecological assessment and pump-station studies are at various stages of completion, and that December flooding again demonstrated the corridor's exposure. Price the prairie as flood land first, mitigation second.

The sub-area a buyer sees is wider than the prairie floor. Cards labelled "Sumas Prairie" include Majuba Hill and Old Yale Road upland acreage — a hillside house on the fringe carries a different flood and slope profile than a farm parcel on the floor, even though both wear the same sub-area label. Check the individual parcel, not the label.
The prairie's board row and its live feed describe different shelves.

The feed's own cards describe septic systems and wells property by property — there is no urban servicing assumption to fall back on, and each system's records have to be pulled for the specific property.
The prairie's parks list on the live page is a list, not a verified guide.

Serviced vs unserviced ground, as the sources state it: feed cards describe septic systems and wells on individual acreage listings (listing text only) — servicing here is per-property (well/septic) on the face of the listings, and servicing for any individual Sumas Prairie property is UNVERIFIED in the research. The same release records that December flooding again demonstrated the corridor is highly prone to water surges, and that the initiative's hydraulic model, risk assessment, ecological assessment and pump-station studies are at various stages of completion — mitigation is active planning, not a settled fix. Live-page land claims NOT carried as verified: the page states the prairie "lies on the former Sumas Lake bed (drained in 1924)" and sits in the City of Abbotsford Floodplain Development Permit Area, protected by the Barrowtown Pump Station and Sumas Dike.
Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals, documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: none is documented in this area's research.

items.t: OCP — CURRENT, with stale citations flagged: Abbotsforward 2050 is the CURRENT Official Community Plan, adopted December 2025.

SSMUH — bylaw number UNCONFIRMED, conflict stated openly: 3560-2024, adopted June 25, 2024" via a program rules-gap note. The bylaw's s.140 provision allows 3 units on lots 280 m² or less and 4 units on lots greater than 280 m² in the stated conditions. How SSMUH applies on ALR prairie parcels is a per-parcel question and is not stated.

ALR block (full — this is dyked-prairie farm ground): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional residence; caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Bare-land strata block (stated for completeness — no Sumas Prairie bare-land strata is verified): Form B (SPA s.59) within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page, with rules, budget and most recent depreciation report attached; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since Jul 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since Nov 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since Nov 24, 2022 (short-term may still be restricted); only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions) — a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. Prairie farm and acreage purchases are fee-simple: NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees.

faq.q: Why can't a prairie farmhouse be bought as strata units?
faq.a: Because ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). On ALR land the housing frame is one principal residence up to 500 m², a suite only inside it, and at most one additional residence of 90 m² (≤40 ha) or 186 m² (>40 ha) — a house on land, never condo lots.

Get the parcel's elevation, Flood Construction Level position and insurance position in writing before subjects come off.
